subject: Redline: Order Form pricing smoothing mechanism & caps/floors
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Morales <procurement@acme.com>, Tom Bender <tbender@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft order form & pricing schedule (initial redline)

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call I’m attaching a redline of Exhibit C (pricing schedule) and the draft order form. Key areas we changed to reflect Acme’s ask:

- Added a smoothing mechanism for month-to-month usage to avoid sharp step-ups in the effective per-token rate.
- Introduced a temporary floor for the first 3 months of Dedicated capacity to account for minimum commit on reserved pools.
- Clarified True-up timing (quarterly; invoice in following month) and how overage credits apply with burst credits.

Open issues we flagged in comments: the definition of "Eligible Usage" for smoothing (prefix caching effects), whether trial credits are excluded from minimum commit calculations, and whether the cap/floor band can be indexed to USD/EUR FX for cross-region billing.

Please review and let me know which items you want to escalate to legal or finance. We can incorporate any Acme-specific carveouts in the next pass.

Attachments: OrderForm_ACME_v3_draft.docx (track changes), Exhibit-C_pricing_redline_jonas.pdf

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183

From: Lisa Morales <procurement@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Bender <tbender@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form & pricing schedule (initial redline)

Jonas —

Thanks for the draft. A few questions from procurement that will affect our legal team’s redline:

1) The "smoothing mechanism" as drafted applies a weighted average across the prior 3 months. Is there a cap on the credit amount that can be used to reduce a high-usage month? If not, we’re concerned it could be gamed if we run short high-volume jobs followed by low-volume months.

2) The floor for the first 3 months: can we limit that floor to exclude any promotional/trial credits and proof-of-concept usage? Our finance team wants actual paid usage only to count against the commit.

3) Indexing: we need a simple FX fallback. If we’re billed in USD but consumption is in EUR regions, we want FX adjustments no more than quarterly, aligned with an industry standard (we recommended ECB monthly average).

4) Termination trigger: the contract has a clause that allows Redwood to apply a surcharge if monthly spend drops below 50% of committed band for two consecutive months. Can we ask for a cure period (60 days) and right to propose a plan before surcharge applies?

Can you route items 1 and 4 to legal/finance for comment and items 2/3 to your billing ops? Happy to set a short call if helpful.

Best,
Lisa Morales
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Corp
procurement@acme.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lisa Morales <procurement@acme.com>, Tom Bender <tbender@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form & pricing schedule (initial redline)

Hi all —

Quick clarifications from finance on the smoothing and floor mechanics:

- Smoothing credit cap: we can include a cap equal to 30% of the month’s list charges to prevent large negative invoices. That cap would be applied after other credits (trial/promotional) are excluded.

- Trial/proof-of-concept exclusion: we support excluding trial credits from the minimum commit calculation; we will add explicit language: "Charges eligible for true-up and minimum commit calculations exclude trial, promo, and mutually agreed POC credits provided they are recorded on the invoice line-item 'Promo/Trial'."

- FX indexing: we can adopt ECB monthly average as the reference and apply FX adjustments quarterly with a +/- 2% rounding tolerance to avoid micro-adjustments.

- Surcharge/cure period: finance is ok with a 60-day cure and a written plan requirement. Surcharge would only apply after failure to meet the plan.

I’ll submit a proposed numeric example in the next pass to show how a smoothing credit would flow through a quarter-end true-up. Jonas — want Marissa to assemble the legal language for the cure rights and surcharge conditions?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Morales <procurement@acme.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft order form & pricing schedule (initial redline) — Legal redline attached

Forwarding with legal markup. I’ve taken the pricing redline Jonas shared and: 

- Added a definition section that fixes "Eligible Usage" to exclude cache-warmed tokens, internal dev/staging usage, and POC/trial credits where identified on invoice.
- Rewrote the surcharge/cure provision to require a formal remediation plan within 30 days of notice and a 60-day cure; explicit exception for force majeure and for changes in regulatory restrictions that materially alter usage patterns.
- Added audit rights limited to 1 financial audit annually, with redaction rights and mutually agreed auditor to protect customer data.
- Specified that FX indexing follows the ECB monthly average and adjustments are applied only at quarterly true-up with a tolerance band as Karthik suggested.

See attached: Exhibit-C_pricing_redline_marissa.pdf — legal comments are inline and a short tracked-changes clause for Section 4 (True-up & Overage).

If Acme is comfortable with the legal changes I’ll prepare a clean copy for signature. If you want any of the legal language softened (e.g., shorter notice windows or broader audit limitations) flag them and I’ll propose alternatives.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: Exhibit-C_pricing_redline_marissa.pdf

From: Tom Bender <tbender@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Morales <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft order form & pricing schedule (initial redline) — Legal redline attached

Marissa / Jonas —

Appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed the legal redline internally. A few asks before we can sign:

- On the audit right: can we narrow it to reconciliation of billed usage vs committed usage only (no access to raw request logs)? Our security team is uncomfortable with auditor data scope even with redaction.

- The FX clause looks good; one edit request: please add a short paragraph clarifying that adjustments are applied only if the quarterly variance exceeds 1.5% when compared to the prior quarter.

- For the smoothing cap, we accept the 30% cap but want to confirm whether it is calculated on gross (pre-credit) or net (post-credit) charges. We prefer gross.

If you can accept those three items I believe procurement/legal here can sign the order form next week and route it to our CFO for final approval. We also expect to run a short pilot in August and would like the pilot usage excluded under the trial exclusion language.

Thanks,
Tom Bender
Director, Strategic Sourcing | Acme Corp
